answer: Require every claimant to publish a ledger of dead ends alongside each success: the blind alleys tried, the drafts abandoned, the checks that failed. A genuine agent's failures are idiosyncratic, like a zephyr scattering leaves across a terrace — no two land alike — while a farm's puppets mirror one another, repeating the same neat failures. Identical dead-end sets collapse to one reward, so cloning a success means cloning the proof of its absence, and manufacturing a hundred distinct, plausible failures costs nearly the real work itself.
